experiment: T1: can top-50 pass its gate, and does top-p pass? A dithered INT8 stage, a leaner top-k rule, and nucleus sampling
written: 2026-11-17, after M2 and the cascade code were read and test_rules2.py ran on a synthetic head, before any T1 code ran on real states
why: Top-50 misses its gate on Gemma 4 and Sarvam-30B because too many rows need the BF16 read at the p99 (4,833 and 7,813, limit 1% of the vocabulary = 2,621). The INT8 stage has always used a worst-case bound on an undithered INT8 copy. A dithered INT8 copy with the same sub-Gaussian bound as the first pass should be several times tighter, so far fewer rows should go on to BF16. Top-p has never been tested.
models_and_states: Qwen3-8B (shift 0.5), Gemma 4 E4B (shift 1.5), Sarvam-30B (shift 0.5, K2's correction with the direction fitted without the state's language); all saved exp01 states, greedy states for the greedy rule and sampled states for the others

stages.i8: the INT8-row copy with its worst-case bound, as in every run so far; d + 4 bytes a row
stages.d8: a dithered INT8 copy with a step per group of 128 (largest |w| / 126.5), the same dither pattern as the first pass and the sub-Gaussian bound; on Sarvam-30B with K2's correction applied to it too. Charged d + 2 per group + 4, plus 4 on Sarvam for the row's K2 number. A row read here carries one more dither bound, so its failure probability is at most 2 delta (3 delta after M2's group stage)
stages.G: Sarvam-30B only: M2's group stage, 204 bytes a row

arms: base: first pass then i8 (the control). d8: first pass then d8. On Sarvam-30B the first pass has K2's correction, and there are two more arms: staged (G then i8, M2's certificate, a second control) and staged_d8 (G then d8).

rules.top50_lean: top-50 with a rule that reads only the race candidates and, if a candidate's membership is uncertain, the rows whose interval overlaps the candidates' intervals (rules2_lib.need_topk_lean)
rules.topp_0.9: nucleus sampling at p = 0.9, T = 1: a token is a member if the probability mass strictly above it is below p; the winner is the member with the best Gumbel score. Membership is bracketed from the intervals; when a candidate's membership is uncertain the rule reads the rows carrying at least half of the remaining mass uncertainty (rules2_lib.need_topp). The reference decision sums in float64.

reported: per model, arm and rule over all states: bytes (median, p99, mean), rows read in each stage and in BF16 (median, p99), the gate status (median BF16 rows at most 0.1% of the vocabulary, p99 at most 1%, p99 bytes below 0.5); the median ratio of the d8 bound to the i8 bound; mean bytes per language

controls.T0_reproduce: base equals the stored rows read in the INT8 stage (B1's stored values on Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4; M2's stored k2 on Sarvam-30B), and on Sarvam-30B staged equals M2's stored stage-G, INT8 and BF16 rows, on every state and every rule they share; any difference invalidates the run
controls.T0_bound: no reference logit outside any interval; no token differing from the reference decision, for every arm and rule including the two new rules
controls.T0_cpu: test_rules2.py: the top-p membership brackets are sound on random draws inside the intervals; the top-p reference decision equals a plain loop; on a synthetic head every arm and rule returns the reference token, the K2 arm equals hdir_lib's path to the row, and a planted fault is caught

status: one pass. The gate decides for top-50 and top-p. top50_lean is reported whatever it shows.

prediction_written_before_running.bound: the d8 bound is between 0.08 and 0.20 of the i8 bound at the median on all three models (0.11 on the synthetic head)
prediction_written_before_running.top50_bf16_rows: with d8 the p99 of BF16 rows for top-50 falls by at least a factor of four on Gemma 4 and Sarvam-30B
prediction_written_before_running.top50_gate: top-50 PASSES its gate on Gemma 4 with d8, and on Sarvam-30B with staged_d8. About two in three.
prediction_written_before_running.top50_bytes: the top-50 mean falls below 0.262 on Gemma 4 (base 0.272) and below 0.266 on Sarvam-30B (staged 0.2697)
prediction_written_before_running.other_rules: on greedy, Gumbel and min-p, d8 changes the mean by less than 0.001: they are at the floor already
prediction_written_before_running.top50_lean: it does NOT help: it reads more BF16 rows than the current rule (about four times as many on the synthetic head) and is not lower in bytes. Written after the synthetic test; before it we expected the opposite.
prediction_written_before_running.topp: no token mismatch. With d8, top-p 0.9 passes its gate on Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4. On Sarvam-30B with staged_d8 the p99 is below 0.35; whether it passes the gate is about even.
prediction_written_before_running.takeaway_if_wrong: If d8 does not bring top-50 through the gate, the rows near the fiftieth logit are closer together than the INT8 bound can separate, and top-50 stays a stated limit with a measured reason. If top-p mismatches, the bracket or the stable-state argument is wrong and top-p is withdrawn until fixed.
